Seventy years of a rivalry that keeps turning, and the 2026 tour

Twelve matches from 22 October: five T20Is, five ODIs and two Tests.

India play five T20Is, five ODIs and two Tests in New Zealand between 22 October and 1 December. It is the largest bilateral tour New Zealand Cricket has ever hosted, and it is set against 100 years of sporting ties between the two countries.

The T20Is are India's first series in New Zealand as double world champions, with Shreyas Iyer now in charge of the side. New Zealand lost the final in Ahmedabad heavily and will want a different story on their own pitches, where the ball swings early and Eden Park's short boundaries punish anything loose.

The ODIs are a meeting of the top two sides in the ICC rankings, a year before the 2027 World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia. New Zealand won the ODI series in India 2-1 in January, so India start this leg with something to put right. Both sides have named separate squads for the first three games and the last two, and Shubman Gill hands the Indian captaincy to Shreyas Iyer for the final two.

The Tests carry the most weight. Both count towards the World Test Championship, where India sit fifth, and New Zealand have won the last three Tests between the sides. India have won a Test series in New Zealand only twice, in 1968 and 2009.

India's T20I squad mixes the World Cup-winning core, including Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson, Axar Patel and Varun Chakaravarthy, with new faces. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and Naman Dhir are in, and Bhuvneshwar Kumar returns, his swing likely to be useful with a new ball in New Zealand.

India have split their ODI squad too. Shubman Gill captains the first three games before he and the Test specialists leave to prepare for Wellington; Shreyas Iyer takes over for the last two. Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli are in for all five. Tilak Varma, Auqib Nabi, Yash Thakur and Kumar Kushagra come in for the final two, and Jasprit Bumrah returns for the Tests.

New Zealand have split their ODI selection. The first three games lean on experience, with Tom Latham, Devon Conway and Rachin Ravindra. The last two bring in pace and power, with Lockie Ferguson, Finn Allen and Tim Seifert, plus uncapped or lightly capped names such as Kristian Clarke, Mitch Hay and Nick Kelly.

Head to head: seventy years of the rivalry

India and New Zealand first played a Test in 1955. The records in Tests, ODIs and T20Is, and the matches that shaped them.

New Zealand arrived in India in late 1955 for a five-Test series and lost it 2-0. In Chennai (then Madras), Vinoo Mankad and Pankaj Roy put on 413 for the first wicket. Twelve years later the roles flipped: Mansur Ali Khan Pataudi's side won 3-1 in New Zealand, India's first Test series win abroad.

Since then the rivalry has swung in long arcs. New Zealand have won the big knockouts as often as India, and India have struggled to win Test series in New Zealand. Start with the numbers, format by format.

For four decades this was a Test contest decided by home conditions: turners in India, seam and wind in New Zealand. India's 1968 series win there took 41 years to repeat.

One-day cricket brought the sides closer. India have won more ODIs, 63 to 52, but New Zealand have tended to rise for the matches that mattered, and since 2019 those have come on the biggest stages.

India lead 104 to 79 across seven decades. That overall number hides three very different contests.

articles.title: Acidente na Rodovia Anhanguera em Jardinópolis causa morte e fogo | G1
articles.standfirst: Trecho foi bloqueado na noite desta quarta-feira (21) e houve congestionamento.
articles.summary: Um motorista morreu após colisão traseira no km 340 da SP-330. O tráfego no sentido Sul foi bloqueado.
articles.body:
Acidente termina em morte e causa interdição na Rodovia Anhanguera em Jardinópolis (SP). — Foto: Portal CCM – ARTESP

Uma colisão entre duas carretas provocou a morte de uma pessoa em um veículo que pegou fogo e a interdição da Rodovia Anhanguera (SP-330), no km 340, em Jardinópolis (SP), na noite desta quarta-feira (21).

Segundo informações do Centro de Controle Operacional (CCO) da concessionária Entrevias, o acidente ocorreu por volta das 19h44, quando uma carreta da Volkswagen atingiu uma carreta Scania.

Com o impacto, a carreta que atingiu a outra pegou fogo e permaneceu sobre a faixa dois da pista. O motorista morreu no local. A carreta que foi atingida parou no acostamento, e o condutor não se feriu.

Devido à gravidade da batida e ao incêndio, as faixas e o acostamento foram bloqueados, gerando ao menos dois quilômetros de congestionamento entre os quilômetros 342 e 340.

As causas da colisão e a identidade do motorista que morreu não tinham sido divulgadas até a última atualização desta reportagem.

articles.body:
Confira como foi a agenda de campanha dos candidatos ao governo do Tocantins nesta quarta-feira (21), no segundo turno das eleições. Professora Dorinha (União Brasil) cumpriu compromissos em Palmas , enquanto Vicentinho Júnior (PSDB) fez campanha em Brejinho de Nazaré, Porto Nacional e Taguatinga.

📱 Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 TO no WhatsApp

Professora Dorinha (União) e Vicentinho Júnior (PSDB) — Foto: Reprodução/TV Anhanguera

A candidata do União Brasil começou o dia participando de uma reunião com lideranças indígenas de diversas etnias. No fim da tarde, esteve no encontro “Todas Por Ela”, onde subiu ao palanque ao lado da senadora pelo Distrito Federal Damares Alves (Republicanos), das senadoras eleitas pelo DF Michelle Bolsonaro (PL) e Bia Kicis (PL), além da primeira-dama do Tocantins, Karynne Sotero.

Durante o evento, Dorinha apresentou prioridades do plano de governo voltadas à proteção e à assistência às mulheres. Entre as propostas, defendeu a ampliação do atendimento policial especializado, com delegacias funcionando 24 horas, ações integradas de combate à violência doméstica e a criação de novas unidades de acolhimento no interior do estado.

“Nós temos a Casa da Mulher Brasileira aqui em Palmas, mas a Casa da Mulher Tocantinense que vai para Araguaína, Gurupi... a estruturação da rede de segurança pública, com o número maior de delegacias, funcionamento 24 horas e, ao mesmo tempo, o programa Antes que Aconteça, o botão do pânico. São ações concretas de combate à violência, aluguel social e a retirada dos agressores das casas das mulheres”, disse a candidata.

Após o evento, Dorinha participou de um encontro com empresários dos setores de engenharia e construção civil, também em Palmas.

O candidato do PSDB participou de uma carreata em Brejinho de Nazaré no início do dia. Ao lado do candidato a vice, Amélio Cayres (MDB), e de apoiadores, ele visitou comerciantes e moradores durante a mobilização.

Em seguida, Vicentinho participou de uma concentração de eleitores em Porto Nacional, município considerado seu reduto político. No local, apresentou propostas do plano de governo voltadas ao desenvolvimento regional.

“Uma dotação orçamentária aprovada na Assembleia de um novo hospital regional de Porto Nacional, que é para atender a saúde da nossa região e que simplesmente se resumiu a um outdoor colocado no anel viário de Porto Nacional. Não lançou-se pedra fundamental, não se iniciou os primeiros alicerces. Então, nós estamos discutindo com a população qual o Tocantins que de fato o tocantinense quer”, afirmou o candidato.

A mobilização em Porto Nacional terminou com uma carreata pelas principais avenidas da cidade e pela Praça do Centenário. Vicentinho encerrou a agenda em Taguatinga, na região sudeste do estado. Durante a noite, participou de reuniões com lideranças políticas e religiosas em Palmas.

articles.title: Eleições 2026: regras para a reta final das campanhas eleitorais visam evitar abusos e manter o equilíbrio entre candidaturas | G1
articles.standfirst: Esta quinta-feira (22), por exemplo, é o último dia permitido para a circulação de propaganda paga ou impulsionada na internet e também para conteúdos de inteligência artificial nas redes sociais.
articles.summary: Esta quinta-feira (22), por exemplo, é o último dia permitido para a circulação de propaganda paga ou impulsionada na internet e também para conteúdos de inteligência artificial nas redes sociais.
articles.body:
Nesta quinta-feira (22), entram em vigor as regras para a reta final das campanhas eleitorais.

O objetivo é evitar abusos e manter o equilíbrio entre as candidaturas. Esta quinta-feira (22) é o último dia permitido para a circulação de propaganda paga ou impulsionada na internet e também para conteúdos de inteligência artificial nas redes sociais. Os comícios das campanhas podem acontecer, no máximo, até as 2h de sexta-feira (23).

A sexta-feira marca o fim da propaganda eleitoral obrigatória no rádio e na TV, da paga na imprensa e dos debates entre os candidatos. No sábado (24), as caminhadas, carreatas, passeatas e a distribuição de material podem ir até as 22h.

Eleições 2026: regras para a reta final das campanhas eleitorais visam evitar abusos e manter o equilíbrio entre candidaturas — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

A lei eleitoral também determina restrições para os chamados CACs - caçadores, atiradores e colecionadores de armas. A partir das 22h de sábado (24), eles estão proibidos de transportar armas e munições em todo o Brasil até a segunda-feira (26), depois das eleições.

No domingo, dia 25, a votação ocorre de 8h às 17h, no horário de Brasília. É proibida boca de urna, como a distribuição de santinhos, bandeiraços, carreatas e comícios. O descumprimento dessas regras pode gerar multas e comprometer a prestação final de contas das campanhas. Os eleitores são essenciais nessa fiscalização e podem denunciar pelo aplicativo chamado Pardal, do TSE.

“É ele que vai votar e é ele quem vai trazer para a Justiça Eleitoral as denúncias relativas às irregularidades nas campanhas. Então, sim, o eleitor baixa o aplicativo Pardal, tira a foto da propaganda irregular na rua, afixada, por exemplo, em equipamentos públicos ou fora do horário permitido, e isso vai ser tratado na comissão de propaganda irregular quanto ao poder de polícia, ir lá e retirar, e também em relação às multas, no aspecto judicial depois, no julgamento dessas representações”, explica Marília Guedes, juíza eleitoral TRE/DF.

articles.title: Prefeito de Nova York chama fim da escala 6x1 de 'passo histórico' no Brasil | G1
articles.standfirst: Prefeito de Nova York relembrou encontro com Lula e disse que construir um futuro melhor passa por devolver às pessoas mais tempo fora do trabalho.
articles.summary: Prefeito de Nova York relembrou encontro com Lula e disse que construir um futuro melhor passa por devolver às pessoas mais tempo fora do trabalho.
articles.body:
Presidente Lula e prefeito de Nova York, Zohran Mamdani, durante encontro na casa do embaixador brasileiro na ONU, Sérgio Danese, em Nova York, nos Estados Unidos, em 21 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Adam Gray/Pool via REUTERS

O prefeito de Nova York, Zohran Mamdani, elogiou nesta quarta-feira (21) a aprovação das novas regras trabalhistas que preveem o fim da escala 6x1 e a redução gradual da jornada semanal no Brasil. Em publicação nas redes sociais, ele atribuiu a medida a uma conquista dos trabalhadores brasileiros e lembrou uma conversa que teve recentemente com o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

"Há um mês, sentei-me com o presidente Lula para discutir como o governo pode servir aos pobres e trabalhadores. Semanas depois, o Brasil deu um passo histórico: uma semana de trabalho de 40 horas, pelo menos dois dias de folga e sem cortes salariais para mais de 30 milhões de trabalhadores", escreveu o prefeito.

Na publicação, Mamdani afirmou que trabalhadores brasileiros e norte-americanos travaram lutas históricas por jornadas menores e mais tempo de descanso.

"Os trabalhadores lutaram por décadas para conquistar a semana de trabalho de cinco dias na América. Os trabalhadores brasileiros também lutaram por esta vitória. Parabenizo-os por esta conquista", declarou.

O prefeito também defendeu a redução do tempo de trabalho como forma de melhorar a qualidade de vida.

"As pessoas que trabalham merecem tempo para viver, não apenas para trabalhar. Construir um futuro melhor significa devolver às pessoas mais de suas vidas", disse.

Publicação do prefeito de Nova York sobre fim da escala 6x1 no Brasil. — Foto: Reprodução/X

A menção a Lula ocorre cerca de um mês após o encontro entre os dois em Nova York , na véspera da Assembleia Geral da ONU. Na ocasião, o presidente brasileiro e o prefeito trocaram presentes, incluindo uma camisa do Corinthians entregue por Lula a Mamdani.

Durante a reunião, realizada na residência do embaixador brasileiro na ONU, os dois conversaram sobre pobreza, desigualdade e o custo de vida nas grandes cidades. Mamdani afirmou que Nova York é uma das cidades mais caras do mundo e disse que um em cada quatro moradores vive na pobreza. Ele também classificou Lula como uma "fonte de inspiração".

Naquele encontro, Lula afirmou esperar que o prefeito se tornasse um "soldado" no combate à pobreza e à invisibilidade social.

A manifestação de Mamdani ocorre poucos dias após a promulgação da PEC que prevê o fim da escala 6x1 . A emenda constitucional garante dois dias de descanso remunerado por semana e estabelece uma redução gradual da jornada de trabalho sem diminuição salarial.

Pelas regras aprovadas, as mudanças começam a valer em 16 de dezembro de 2026. A partir dessa data, a jornada máxima passará de 44 para 42 horas semanais, com dois dias de descanso remunerado por semana. Em 16 de dezembro de 2027, o limite será reduzido para 40 horas semanais.

Segundo o texto promulgado pelo Congresso, a redução ocorrerá sem corte de salários e deverá beneficiar 14,8 milhões de trabalhadores brasileiros.

articles.title: How a domestic dispute led 2 brothers to strangle their father, burn his body with petrol and bury it near home
articles.summary: Jhunjhunu police arrested brothers Shiv and Deependra Jangid for allegedly killing father Jugal Kishore, burning the body with petrol and burying it.
articles.body: JHUNJHUNU: Police Tuesday arrested two brothers for allegedly strangling their father, burning his body with petrol and burying it near their house at Tara ka Bas village in Jhunjhunu’s Sultana police station area.Sultana SHO Ramniwas said preliminary investigation indicated that Shiv and Deependra had allegedly killed their father, Jugal Kishore Jangid, during a domestic dispute. They allegedly told relatives and others that he had gone to Mumbai and claimed that the buried remains belonged to an unidentified person.Police received information on Oct 17, 2026 about a body buried near a house in the village. An FSL team examined the site, and the body was identified as Jugal Kishore.His cousin, Pawan Kumar, lodged a report on Oct 18. Questioning of family members revealed that Jugal Kishore had been missing for six to seven days. Police registered a case on suspicion that he had been murdered and buried.Chirawa DSP Gaurav Gurjar inspected the scene, while MIU and MOB teams collected scientific evidence. A team led by Ramniwas investigated the case using technical evidence and intelligence inputs.Police said suspicion subsequently fell on Jugal Kishore’s sons. They were detained for questioning and arrested after facts concerning the incident emerged.According to Ramniwas, the brothers allegedly strangled their father in a fit of rage, poured petrol on his body, burnt it and buried it in the soil near their house. The killing was believed to have occurred five to seven days before the body was found.A court remanded both accused in police custody for three days. articles.title: In Pakistan, Maldives President Mohamed Muizzu calls for early Saarc summit
articles.summary: In remarks likely to ruffle feathers in India, Maldives President Mohamed Muizzu called for an early convening of the Saarc summit during his visit to
articles.body: In remarks likely to ruffle feathers in India, Maldives President Mohamed Muizzu called for an early convening of the Saarc summit during his visit to Pakistan, saying Male is ready to work with other member-states to make the summit happen.The summit, which was to take place in Islamabad in 2016, was called off because of the cross-border Uri terrorist attack in J&K and the process has remained stalled since then. India maintains that regional cooperation under Saarc is possible only in an atmosphere free of terror and it’s up to Pakistan to create that environment.Maldives and Pak sign 20 MoUs including defence, maritime cooperationI believe that through this organisation, we can work together to find solutions to the challenges facing the countries of this region,” said Muizzu in Islamabad during what was the first visit by a Maldivian president to Pakistan in over a decade.“The Maldives stands ready to consult with member countries on resuming Saarc’s work. Through sustained dialogue, trust and understanding, we can strengthen cooperation within Saarc,” he said.The visit also saw the two sides signing 20 MoUs, including in areas like defence and maritime cooperation that will be of concern to India.This is not the first time though that Muizzu has called for revival of Saarc. In his independence day speech this year, Muizzu had also offered to act as a mediator between India and Pakistan to advance talks for an early leaders’ summit.The last Saarc summit was held in 2014 in Nepal. Member-states like the Maldives, Bangladesh and Nepal have from time-to-time sought revival of the summit.In its response, India has always blamed Pakistan for blocking the initiative for a connected and integrated South Asia.“India favours strong regional cooperation and has been working towards it for several decades. Everyone in South Asia is aware of which country and what activities are responsible for stymieing Saarc,” said MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal, responding to media queries on Muizzu’s remarks in July.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘Racial attack’ by Delhi influencer on tribal youth roils Tripura
articles.summary: AGARTALA/NEW DELHI: Political parties in Tripura closed ranks Wednesday over the alleged racial harassment in Delhi of a tribal youth from Gomati district
articles.body: AGARTALA/NEW DELHI: Political parties in Tripura closed ranks Wednesday over the alleged racial harassment in Delhi of a tribal youth from Gomati district and demanded legal action against social media influencer Amir Shokeen after a video purportedly showing him taunting the young man over his ethnicity circulated online.The clip, which surfaced Tuesday evening, purportedly shows Shokeen asking the youth if he is the "president" of a neighbouring country. He allegedly also mocks Tripura when the man responds he is Indian.CM Manik Saha of BJP directed the Tripura DGP to coordinate with Delhi Police and ensure a proper probe. CPM state secretary and lead-er of the opposition Jitendra Chaudhury demanded Shokeen apologise."Establish a precedent that is both resounding and unmistakable, ensuring no one ever dares insult Tripura and the Tiprasa community again," he said.Congress MLA Sudip Roy Barman called for a joint protest in Delhi. "This type of attitude is intolerable," he said.After TIPRA Motha chief Pradyot Kishore Debbarman called on the party's youth and students' wings to act, Youth Tipra Federation lodged a complaint accusing Shokeen of hate speech and defamatory remarks."Shokeen made crude and vulgar remarks..., calling him 'Chinese' and made fun of our state's name," said James Debbarma, general sec-retary of Youth Tipra Federation and an elected member of the Tripura tribal areas autonomous district council.Members of Twipra Students' Federation plan to meet the Delhi Police commissioner Thursday. "We are trying to identify the boy who was harassed and file a complaint," said general secretary Hamalu Jamatia.Shokeen has put out a video on Facebook claiming it was scripted. He said the target of his alleged abuse was an acquaintance who worked at a friend's cafe in Ahmedabad. articles.title: Mumbai clears 77 of 231 garbage hotspots, targets 128 by year-end
articles.summary: MUMBAI: From reclaiming footpaths riddled with illegal construction debris to creating seating areas for senior citizens, BMC is attempting to turn
articles.body: MUMBAI: From reclaiming footpaths riddled with illegal construction debris to creating seating areas for senior citizens, BMC is attempting to turn Mumbai's garbage-vulnerable points (GVPs) into usable public spaces.Of the 231 such spots identified across the city till April this year, 77 had been cleaned up by Oct, leaving 154. The civic body has set a target of bringing the number down to 128 by Dec. A garbage-vulnerable point is a location where waste is repeatedly dumped and accumulates over a prolonged period, requiring intervention by the concerned civic ward to address the problem.Two such locations are in Sewri and Chinchpokli areas wherein the civic body is attempting to go beyond simply clearing accumulated waste. At Zakaria Bunder Road along Eastern Freeway, a spot where construction and demolition (C&D) waste was being dumped illegally at night has been cleared, restoring the footpath for safer and more convenient pedestrian movement.A CCTV now has been placed there as well. Shiv Sena UBT corporator Bharti Pednekar said at Chinchpokli, another GVP has been eliminated and the space converted into a seating area, with benches now placed at the site. "The facility gives elderly residents a place to sit, relax and interact with one another. We have even spoken to the locals to ensure they dispose waste the correct way," she said.However, sustaining these improvements remains a challenge, particularly in neighbourhoods where dumping garbage at the same location has become a long-standing practice. Assistant Municipal Commissioner of F-South ward Vrushali Ingole said eliminating GVPs requires residents to cooperate with the civic body and hand over their waste directly to BMC collection vans rather than dumping it on roadsides."The ward first deploys staff at an identified spot for a few days to understand where the garbage is coming from. Our teams then approach residents in the surrounding areas, explain the need to stop dumping waste at the location and seek their cooperation. We have also arranged for collection vans to stop at convenient points so residents can hand over their garbage directly," she said.Sanjay Mohite, assistant engineer of F-South's solid waste department, said at the Eastern Freeway location, the ward set up a Solid Waste Management chowky to ensure staff presence and prevent the spot from reverting to a dumping ground. "The footpath was also improved and greenery added to discourage fresh dumping. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and external affairs minister S Jaishankar on Thursday extended birthday wishes to Union home minister Amit Shah as he turned 62, praising his commitment to national security and public welfare.In a post on X, PM Modi said Shah's administrative understanding had made India's internal security systems more effective. Particularly noteworthy are the successes in eliminating the menace of Maoism and in furthering our dream of a society free from drugs. I pray that he is blessed with a long and healthy life in service of the people," he said.Jaishankar also extended birthday greetings to Shah, saying his commitment to national security and public welfare was commendable. He prayed for Shah's good health, happiness and long life."Heartfelt birthday wishes to the Union Home and Cooperation Minister Shri Amit Shah. Your commitment to national security and public welfare is commendable. I pray to God for your good health, a happy life, and long life," he said.Defence minister Rajnath Singh too extended his wishes saying: "Heartfelt birthday wishes to my colleague in the Union Cabinet, Union home and cooperation minister Shri Amit Shah. articles.title: ‘Anti-Indian hate is exploding’: US lawmaker Raja Krishnamoorthi flags rising anti-Hindu hate online
articles.summary: US Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi on Wednesday (local time) raised concerns over rising anti-Indian, anti-South Asian and anti-Hindu hate on social
articles.body: US Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi on Wednesday (local time) raised concerns over rising anti-Indian, anti-South Asian and anti-Hindu hate on social media, accusing major technology companies of profiting from online hostility and calling on Congress to hold them accountable.In a post on X, Krishnamoorthi said, "Anti-Indian hate is exploding on social media, and Big Tech is profiting from it. These companies have no incentive to stop the hatred they help spread. Congress must hold them accountable."He alleged that social media platforms were failing to adequately monitor hateful content, citing an increase of more than 240 per cent in posts promoting anti-South Asian hate.In a video attached to the post, Krishnamoorthi said, "Big Tech is not policing their social media platforms where there's been an explosion of anti-South Asian, anti-Indian, anti-Hindu hate. I'll just give you one statistic: the number of X posts, posts on X or tweets, basically touting anti-South Asian hate has increased by more than 240 per cent over a very short period of time.""And, unfortunately, Big Tech is profiting off of this hate. They have no incentive right now to decrease it. And so we have to at this point, at the federal level, make sure that they face the full consequences of not taking action," he added.His remarks come amid growing concerns over online hostility towards South Asian communities and follow an attempted shooting at the Sri Venkateswara Swami (Balaji) Hindu temple in Aurora, Illinois, on October 11.Krishnamoorthi was worshipping at the temple with his family when the alleged attack took place. He subsequently led 105 members of Congress, including every Indian American member of Congress, in urging FBI director Kash Patel to investigate the incident as a potential federal hate crime.According to prosecutors, 19-year-old Alexandros Paporakis, a self-identified neo-Nazi, allegedly attempted to shoot a man outside the temple, but his rifle jammed. He fled the scene and later communicated plans to return. A coworker alerted the police, who arrested him that day.Prosecutors allege that Paporakis had authored an eight-page white supremacist manifesto describing violence against people of Indian descent at a Hindu place of worship.In their letter to Patel, the lawmakers wrote, "The alleged combination of targeted racial hatred, a religious setting, and preparations for mass violence demands a comprehensive federal response. We appreciate the FBI’s reported assistance to local investigators and urge the Bureau to ensure that potential hate-crime violations receive explicit attention."The lawmakers also sought details on whether the FBI was examining possible racial, ethnic and religious bias in the Aurora case, whether online platforms or other individuals had facilitated the alleged plot, and what measures the Bureau was taking to address credible threats against Indian Americans, Hindu Americans and other South Asian communities.The letter further stated, "We believe such messaging risks lending governmental legitimacy to racial and religious stereotyping. Federal agencies should make clear that debates over immigration or public safety never justify collective suspicion of Indian, Sikh, Hindu, or other South Asian communities."The lawmakers requested a written response to their questions by October 29, to the extent permitted by the ongoing investigation.Krishnamoorthi flags polarisation in the USEarlier, on October 20, Krishnamoorthi told news agency ANI that the US was becoming increasingly polarised, alleging that rhetoric from senior government officials was contributing to hostility towards minority communities."Well, yes, I do think that the America of today is more polarised than ever before," he said. He added that leaders at the highest levels of government were targeting groups, including Muslims, Indians and gay people, and "villainising people".Citing a controversial post by the department of homeland security targeting a Sikh man, Krishnamoorthi said, "I mean, the best example of that was the Department of Homeland Security tweet on their official account targeting a quote, unquote, 'Mr. Singh,' and saying, you know, 'self-deport or else. And predictably, one week later, a gentleman named Mr. Singh, a Sikh truck driver, was stabbed 17 times, came within inches of his life."The DHS post, which was later deleted, featured a Transformers-themed cartoon depicting an Indian Sikh man alongside the phrase "Get off our roads, you don’t know how to drive Mr. Singh” and the words “Self deport or find out".Calling for action against hate crimes, Krishnamoorthi said, "And this is what has to stop. If we're going to stop this horrible rash of hate, it has to stop at the top.""And once that happens, I think things become better, although we at all levels of government have to stand together against it," he added.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
